description: Survey/questions and ingredient measurement/evidence requirements. A question is not a completed rating, verified clinical advantage or investor forecast.

assessments.name: Patient Population
assessments.objective: Eligible treated patients by jurisdiction, age, disease stage, biomarkers, prior therapy and treatment line.

ingredients.label: Eligible U.S. Patients
ingredients.question: Estimate the number of patients who could actually qualify for treatment, not merely total disease prevalence.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated U.S. epidemiology, diagnosis rates, label-eligible subsets and exclusions.

ingredients.label: Best-Responding Patient Subgroup
ingredients.question: Identify patient characteristics and biomarkers associated with supported incremental benefit.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Predefined subgroup analyses, interaction tests and population size.

assessments.name: Unmet Medical Need
assessments.objective: Document residual burden, current treatment gaps, refractory and intolerant populations.

ingredients.label: Current Standard of Care
ingredients.question: Identify the treatments patients currently receive and the appropriate comparison.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Contemporary clinical guidelines, current FDA labels and treatment share.

ingredients.label: Unmet Medical Need
ingredients.question: Determine how many patients remain inadequately treated by existing options.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Residual symptom burden, treatment failure and eligible untreated or refractory population.

ingredients.label: Treatment-Resistant Patient Advantage
ingredients.question: Assess benefit for patients with prior failures or intolerance to available treatment.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Refractory subgroup eligibility, comparator and confirmed benefit.

assessments.name: Clinical Benefit
assessments.objective: Source endpoints, effect sizes, significance, durability and patient-important differences.

ingredients.label: Clinical Patient Benefit
ingredients.question: Explain exactly what improves for patients compared with existing treatment, and by how much.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Matched endpoints, effect size, comparator, follow-up and uncertainty, not a p-value alone.

ingredients.label: Magnitude of Clinical Improvement
ingredients.question: Measure absolute and relative differences in patient-important outcomes against a valid comparator.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Matched effect sizes, units, follow-up and confidence intervals.

ingredients.label: Clinically Meaningful Benefit
ingredients.question: Distinguish patient-important improvements from statistical significance alone.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Disease-specific clinical relevance threshold and prespecified patient outcomes.

ingredients.label: Durability of Treatment Effect
ingredients.question: Determine how long treatment response, remission or clinical benefit is maintained.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Matched follow-up windows, sustained response curves and censoring.

ingredients.label: Responder / Remission Advantage
ingredients.question: Compare the share of patients reaching clinically meaningful response or remission.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Same responder definition, denominator and follow-up time.

ingredients.label: Time to Treatment Response
ingredients.question: Measure how quickly patients experience meaningful improvement.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Comparator-aligned onset endpoint, median time and uncertainty.

assessments.name: Survival Benefit
assessments.objective: Where applicable, evaluate OS/PFS, mortality, hazard ratio, follow-up and uncertainty; do not infer benefit otherwise.

ingredients.label: Survival Benefit Evidence
ingredients.question: Assess survival only when applicable; distinguish overall survival from progression endpoints.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Prespecified OS/PFS estimand, event counts, hazard ratio and confidence interval, absolute survival, censoring and follow-up.

assessments.name: Quality-of-Life Improvement
assessments.objective: Use validated patient-reported outcomes, daily functioning and minimal clinically important differences.

ingredients.label: Quality-of-Life Improvement
ingredients.question: Compare validated patient-reported outcomes, functioning and daily-life effects.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Validated scales, clinically important difference and missing-data impact.

assessments.name: Competitive Advantage
assessments.objective: Compare approved and pipeline competitors by matched indication, line and population; distinguish direct vs indirect comparisons.

ingredients.label: Closest Competing Therapy
ingredients.question: Identify the most relevant existing or developing treatment for the same indication and line of therapy.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Current FDA label, guideline, eligibility overlap and line of treatment.

ingredients.label: Number of Competitors
ingredients.question: Count competing approved treatments and late-stage therapies separately, using the same indication and patient population.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Deduplicated drug-indication comparison, approved FDA labels and current Phase 3 pipeline; exclude same-drug duplicate trials.

ingredients.label: Head-to-Head Evidence
ingredients.question: Determine whether a direct comparison shows superiority or noninferiority to the closest relevant therapy.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Randomized comparator details, predefined estimand, endpoints, results and uncertainty.

ingredients.label: Competitive Pipeline Threat
ingredients.question: Identify late-stage challengers for the same patient group and material upcoming events.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Unique comparator programs, trial status, readout dates and labels.

ingredients.label: Competitive Strategies
ingredients.question: Rank the therapy’s evidence-supported competitive advantages from strongest to weakest.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Rank each comparator-specific advantage with sources, magnitude and counterarguments; generic priorities are unscored.

assessments.name: Treatment Convenience
assessments.objective: Compare administration route, frequency, care setting, monitoring, treatment line and adherence.

ingredients.label: Treatment Convenience
ingredients.question: Compare dosing frequency, route, treatment burden, and monitoring.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Current vs proposed regimen, route, frequency, monitoring and persistence.

ingredients.label: Place in Treatment Sequence
ingredients.question: Identify whether the therapy is suitable for first-line, later-line or post-failure treatment.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Proposed indication, pivotal trial population and guideline sequencing.

assessments.name: Safety Advantage
assessments.objective: Compare relevant adverse events, serious risks and discontinuation with exposure-aligned denominators.

ingredients.label: Safety Advantage
ingredients.question: Compare adverse effects, serious risks, and treatment discontinuation.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Comparable safety populations, follow-up and clinically relevant adverse events.

ingredients.label: Serious Adverse Event Difference
ingredients.question: Compare serious adverse events and treatment-associated risks against relevant therapy.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Exposure-adjusted comparable SAE rates, attribution and follow-up.

ingredients.label: Treatment Discontinuation Difference
ingredients.question: Compare stops due to adverse events, treatment burden or lack of effect.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Similar follow-up and denominators with reason-coded discontinuations.

assessments.name: Healthcare Cost Savings
assessments.objective: Assess patient-important cost offsets, hospitalizations, treatment cost differences and value per outcome.

ingredients.label: Hospitalization / Complication Reduction
ingredients.question: Measure prevention of hospital admission, complications or disability.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Patient-relevant outcomes, event rates and comparator-adjusted effect.

ingredients.label: Treatment Cost Advantage
ingredients.question: Compare equivalent first-year treatment costs and explain the difference.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated comparable price basis and 12-month drug plus monitoring/administration regimen costs.

ingredients.label: Value per Clinical Outcome
ingredients.question: Compare added medical benefit with the incremental cost of treatment.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Comparable cost bases, outcome measures, time horizon and sensitivity analysis.

assessments.name: Insurance Coverage Potential
assessments.objective: Source coverage policy, payer barriers and reimbursement conditions; distinguish prospective from active coverage.

ingredients.label: Insurance / Access
ingredients.question: Determine whether coverage, reimbursement, and prescribing restrictions may limit adoption.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Payer policy, formulary, prior authorization, patient copays and access date.

assessments.name: Expected Treatment Price
assessments.objective: Source or explicitly model comparable net treatment pricing, duration and payer basis; no unsourced launch prices.

ingredients.label: Expected Treatment Price
ingredients.question: Document an observed price or an explicitly modeled price scenario.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated payer/price disclosure, territory, currency, gross versus net basis, dosing and treatment duration.

assessments.name: Market Penetration
assessments.objective: Model uptake from the actual eligible patient pool, treatment switching and addressable starts.

ingredients.label: Projected Adoption
ingredients.question: Estimate the proportion of eligible patients who could receive the new therapy over time.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: 12/24/36-month adoption assumptions, eligible denominator, switching, new starts, coverage and confidence.

ingredients.label: Switching-Eligible Patient Pool
ingredients.question: Estimate how many patients on current treatments could appropriately switch.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Indication overlap, contraindications, switching evidence and treated denominators.

assessments.name: International Patient Population
assessments.objective: Break down eligible non-US populations and separate foreign regulatory and reimbursement status.

ingredients.label: International Eligible Patients
ingredients.question: Estimate eligible patients outside the U.S. without summing overlapping populations.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Country-specific epidemiology, diagnosis and label eligibility, treatment line, year and reimbursement constraints.

assessments.name: Additional Indications
assessments.objective: Track adjacent indication-specific trial programs, distinct NCTs and required regulatory pathways.

ingredients.label: Additional Indication Programs
ingredients.question: Document distinct indication-specific expansion programs separately from the index program.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Exact additional NCT, sponsor/product, indication, phase and jurisdiction; no assumed approval or probability.

assessments.name: Peak Annual Sales
assessments.objective: Use explicit low/base/high uptake × net price × duration calculations and source territorial rights.

ingredients.label: Peak Annual Sales Scenarios
ingredients.question: Model transparent scenarios rather than assert an unsupported forecast.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Eligible population, adoption, net price, duration, territory and commercial rights, each with a source and assumptions.

assessments.name: Revenue Growth Potential
assessments.objective: Model launch ramp, new starts, persistence, price and competition over time with scenarios.

ingredients.label: Revenue Growth Scenarios
ingredients.question: Show launch ramp and revenue growth with explicit time horizons.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated issuer revenue baseline, launch timing, new starts, persistence, pricing and competition assumptions.

assessments.name: Patent and Exclusivity Value
assessments.objective: Check patent claims, expiry, regulatory exclusivity, challenges and market-entry timing.

ingredients.label: Commercial Exclusivity Advantage
ingredients.question: Evaluate relevant intellectual-property and regulatory exclusivity constraints.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated FDA exclusivity records, patent claims, term and litigation caveats.

assessments.name: Licensing and Partnership Value
assessments.objective: Check geographic commercial rights, partner identity, royalties, milestone and SEC agreement details.

ingredients.label: Licensing and Partnership Economics
ingredients.question: Reconcile contractual value to the exact product, indication and territory.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: SEC-filed material agreement, partners, territorial rights, royalties, milestones, obligations and termination terms.

assessments.name: Company Valuation Impact
assessments.objective: Model product-level risk-adjusted value versus enterprise value, dilution and assets; separate FDA probability.

ingredients.label: Company Valuation Impact
ingredients.question: Separate product valuation scenarios from clinical assessment and FDA probability.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated enterprise value inputs, product cash-flow assumptions, cash/debt, rights, discounting and dilution.

assessments.name: Shareholder Upside and Risk
assessments.objective: Model bear/base/bull scenarios, financing, liquidity and dilution without implying a trade recommendation.

ingredients.label: Shareholder Upside and Risk Scenarios
ingredients.question: Document bear/base/bull outcomes, liquidity and dilution without a trading recommendation.
ingredients.evidenceRequirement: Dated share count, cash runway, debt, financing terms, scenario assumptions and counterevidence.
